result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.is_simple_path()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Check if a sequence of nodes forms a simple path in the graph. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L18682-L18834){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.is_simple_path(nodes) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} A simple path is a sequence where: 1. all nodes exist in the graph 2. each consecutive pair of nodes is connected by an edge 3. no node appears more than once (no cycles) This is a fast `O(n)` validation method useful for checking user input, validating computed paths, or testing path properties. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [nodes]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [list[Union[int, str]]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Sequence of node IDs or labels to validate. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : `True` if the sequence forms a valid simple path, `False` otherwise. ::: ## Algorithm {.doc-algorithm} - time complexity: `O(n)` where n is the length of the node sequence - space complexity: `O(n)` for tracking visited nodes - checks performed: node existence, edge connectivity, no repetitions ## Common Use Cases {.doc-common-use-cases} - input validation: check user-provided paths before processing - path verification: validate paths returned by algorithms - route Checking: verify delivery or travel routes - graph Algorithms: test path properties in custom algorithms - debugging: verify intermediate results in path computations ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} Validation runs in a single pass through the sequence in $O(n)$: each node is checked for existence, each consecutive pair for an edge in the required direction, and a visited set ensures no repetition. Enumerating all simple paths first and then testing membership would work but is dramatically slower for graphs of nontrivial size. Edge cases behave the way graph theory would predict: empty sequences and single-node sequences count as valid (trivial) simple paths. Node IDs and labels can be mixed in the same sequence and the resolver picks the right one for each element. ## Examples {.doc-examples} In a simple path `A -- B -- C`, only sequences that follow real edges without repeating a node are valid: ::: {#caf80e29 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_node(label="C") .add_edge("A", "B") .add_edge("B", "C") ) # Returns True graph.is_simple_path(["A", "B", "C"]) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` True ``` ::: ::: ::: {#7f9a9b4a .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} # Returns False: there is no direct edge from A to C graph.is_simple_path(["A", "C"]) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` False ``` ::: ::: A sequence that revisits a node is rejected even if every step follows a real edge, which is how the method distinguishes simple paths from cycles: ::: {#18be845e .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_node(label="C") .add_edge("A", "B") .add_edge("B", "C") .add_edge("C", "A") ) # Returns True graph.is_simple_path(["A", "B", "C"]) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` True ``` ::: ::: ::: {#31052706 .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} # Returns False: A appears twice graph.is_simple_path(["A", "B", "C", "A"]) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ``` False ``` ::: ::: Because this check is much cheaper than enumerating paths, it's a good way to validate paths returned by `get_all_simple_paths()`: ::: {#266ff763 .cell execution_count=5} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_node(label="C") .add_node(label="D") .add_edge(source="A", target="B") .add_edge(source="B", target="C") .add_edge(source="C", target="D") ) paths = graph.get_all_simple_paths("A", "D") # Returns True for every path found all(graph.is_simple_path(path) for path in paths) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=5} ``` True ``` ::: ::: Empty and single-node sequences are treated as trivially valid, as long as the single node actually exists: ::: {#594598a2 .cell execution_count=6} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_edge(source="A", target="B") ) # Returns (True, True, False) ( graph.is_simple_path([]), graph.is_simple_path(["A"]), graph.is_simple_path(["Z"]), ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=6} ``` (True, True, False) ``` ::: :::
